 Need assistance? Our obituary desk is here to help. Please call us at 651-228-5263 with any questions regarding the process or deadlines.
General Information:

 Phone number,
 And an alternate phone number (if any)
Obituary Specification:

 A photo in a JPEG or PDF file is preferable, TIF and other files are accepted, we will contact you if there are any issues with the photo.
 Ad Run dates
 There is a discount for running more than one day, but this must be scheduled on the first run date to apply.
 If a photo is used, it must be used for both days for the discount to apply, contact us for more information.
Policies:
Verification of Death:
In order to publish obituaries a name and phone number of funeral home/cremation society is required. We must contact the funeral home/cremation society handling the arrangements during their business hours to verify the death. If the body of the deceased has been donated to the University of Minnesota Anatomy Bequest Program, or a similar program, their phone number is required for verification.
Please allow enough time to contact them especially during their limited weekend hours.
A death certificate is also acceptable for this purpose but only one of these two options are necessary.
Guestbook and Outside Websites:
We are not allowed to reference other media sources with a guestbook or an obituary placed elsewhere when placing an obituary in print and online. We may place a website for a funeral home or a family email for contact instead; contact us with any questions regarding this matter.
Obituary Process:
Once your submission is completed, we will fax or email a proof for review prior to publication in the newspaper. This proof includes price and days the notice is scheduled to appear.
 Please review the proof carefully. We must be notified of errors or changes before the notice appears in the Pioneer Press based on each day’s deadlines.
After publication, we will not be responsible for errors that may occur after final proofing.
Online:
Changes to an online obituary can be handled through the obituary desk. Call us with further questions.
Payment Procedure:
Pre-payment is required for all obituary notices prior to publication by the deadline specified below in our deadline schedule. Please call 651-228-5263 with your payment information after you have received the proof and approved its contents.
 Credit Card: Payment accepted by phone only due to PCI (Payment Card Industry) regulations
 EFT: Check by phone. Please provide your routing number and account number.
Rates:
 The minimum charge is $162 for the first 12 lines.
 Every line after the first 12 is $12.
 If the ad is under 12 lines it will be charged the minimum rate of $162.
 Obituaries including more than 40 lines will receive a 7.5% discount per line.
 On a second run date, receive a 20% discount off both the first and second placement.
 Place three obituaries and the third placement will be free of charge.
 Each photo published is $125 per day. For example: 2 photos in the paper on 2 days would be 4 photo charges at $500.

 ANN ARBOR, MICHIGAN – OCTOBER 24: Head coach Curt Cignetti of the Indiana Hoosiers looks on while playing the Michigan Wolverines at Michigan Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) 
 By Andy Greder | agreder@pioneerpress.com | Pioneer Press PUBLISHED: October 30, 2026 at 10:24 AM CDT | UPDATED: October 31, 2026 at 6:37 AM CDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... MINNESOTA at INDIANA
 When: 2:30 p.m CT Saturday
 Where: Memorial Stadium, Bloomington, Ind.
 Stream: CBS
 Radio: KFXN-100.3 FM
 Weather: 64 degrees, overcast, 7 mph east wind
 Betting spread: Indiana, minus-20.5
 Records: The Gophers (5-2, 3-1 Big Ten) edged then-No. 15 Iowa 13-10 at home to win Floyd of Rosedale for the second time in four years. No. 4 Indiana (7-1, 3-1) outlasted Michigan 13-6 in overtime in Ann Arbor, Mich., last weekend.
 Context: Based on combined winning percentage, the Gophers have the toughest remaining schedule in the country. Their next five opponents — Indiana, UCLA, Penn State, Northwestern and Wisconsin —  are a combined 28-8 (.778), and Penn State has half those losses.
 History: The Gophers are 40-26-3 all-time against Indiana, including wins in the last four. But they have not played the Hoosiers with head coach Curt Cignetti. At Indiana, he is 34-3, 19-1 at home, his team went 16-0 to win the national championship last season. Minnesota is 0-12 against reigning national champions, including Ohio State last year and Michigan in 2024.
 Big question: Can the Gophers compete with a College Football Playoff contender? Against top 10 teams last season, Minnesota lost to No. 1 Ohio State and No. 7 Oregon by a combined 84-16. Those games were over by halftime.
 RELATED: Hoosiers have one of “most disruptive” pass rushes in country 
 Key matchup: Gophers offense vs. Indiana defense.
 Indiana has been elite. They are tied for second in the nation in two key categories: 12.0 points per game and 4.14 yards allowed per play.
 Meanwhile, Minnesota’s offense has been … ehh. They are outside the top 80 in those same categories.
 The U’s running game is stuck in the mud, and quarterback Drake Lindsey has been inconsistent. After setting a program record for attempts without an interception, the junior has six picks in the past five games. He is 15th in the Big Ten in efficiency (127.2).
 “He just has to know the windows are smaller and guys might not be as open as they are in certain other games,” offensive coordinator Greg Harbaugh said. “(It’s about) raising your level of play when you play against these high-level defenses like an Indiana.”
 Key to the game: Indiana has won or tied the turnover margin in 32 straight games — the most in FBS since at least 1995. Minnesota’s plus-three in turnover margin against Iowa helped them win as a seven-point underdog. Minnesota will need to snap Indiana’s streak if the U is to win as three-touchdown underdog.
 Key injuries:  Gophers defensive tackle Riley Sunram is probable to play, while tight end Pierce Walsh and safety Garison Monroe are out.
 Hoosiers quarterback Josh Hoover, who presumably has a shoulder injury, is probable.
 Players to watch: Cornerback John Nestor is the highest-graded cornerback this season, per Pro Football Focus. and he was named the Senior Bowl’s defensive player of the week for 11 tackles and one forced fumble against Iowa.
 “Unbelievable season,” defensive coordinator Danny Collins said.
 But Nestor and fellow corner Aydan West will have their hands full with Hoosiers wideouts Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh, the best duo in the conference.
 Tidbit:  ESPN’s College GameDay is in Bloomington, Ind., this week, a nice spotlight for the Gophers. It’s only the third time the U has been at the site of the popular pregame show and a first on the road.
 Prediction: Minnesota has wins against three ranked opponents this year but has not proven under Fleck it can hang with the best of the best. The Gophers’ subpar offensive play won’t change that this year. Indiana, 27-13.
